headline: Mandatory Daily Vehicle Permits for Beach Access
reservation: Daily Vehicle Permits (DVP) are mandatory for entry and should be reserved up to five days in advance via the Ontario Parks website to guarantee access. Separate reservations are required for camping at sites like Outlet River or Cedar Ridge, which are often fully booked for the summer by early spring.

days.title: Dunes and Sand Formations

stops.name: Dunes Beach
stops.detail: Explore the world's largest formation of baymouth barrier dunes, featuring a trail through unique pannes and sand slopes.

stops.name: West Lake
stops.detail: Enjoy the shallower, warmer waters protected by the dune system, ideal for viewing the sunset over the water.

days.driving: Allow 20 minutes; local county roads have lower speed limits
days.note: The dunes are fragile; visitors must stay on marked boardwalks and trails.

days.title: Coastal Shorelines and Swimming

stops.name: Outlet Beach
stops.detail: Visit this long, sandy expanse on Lake Ontario, popular for its gentle slope and swimming areas.

stops.name: Cedar Sands Trail
stops.detail: Walk this 2km loop through the woods along the Outlet River, highlighting the local ecology and cedar forests.

days.driving: Allow 15 minutes; internal park roads can be slow
days.note: Lifeguards are not present at all beaches; water safety is the responsibility of the visitor.

days.title: Heritage and Backcountry Borders

stops.name: Lakeshore Beach
stops.detail: Explore the rockier and quieter sections of the coast, often featuring diverse birdlife during migration seasons.

stops.name: Sandbanks Estate and Historical Markers
stops.detail: Learn about the early settlement history and the efforts to stabilize the moving sands in the early 20th century.

days.driving: Allow 30 minutes; varies with entrance gate queues
days.note: Check the official park Twitter or website for beach capacity alerts before leaving your gateway city.

intel.title: Lot Capacity Logic
intel.text: Parking is tied to your Daily Vehicle Permit for a specific zone. Once a lot is full, even permit holders may need to wait for a space to vacate.

intel.title: Rural Connectivity
intel.text: Cellular coverage is generally strong across Prince Edward County, though signal strength can dip in the middle of the dunes or near the swampier pannes.

intel.title: Gateway Fueling
intel.text: Fuel and supplies must be secured in Picton, Wellington, or Bloomfield. There are no gas stations within the provincial park boundaries.

intel.title: Permit Entry Windows
intel.text: Permits typically allow entry during park operating hours. Early arrival is suggested to maximize your day, as queues at the main gate can form by mid-morning.

intel.title: Dog-Free and Pet Zones
intel.text: Specific sections of the beach are designated as pet-free to protect the environment and visitors. Check the current park map for designated dog-friendly swimming areas.

plan.arrival: Drive from Toronto or Ottawa, stopping in Belleville for major groceries before entering Prince Edward County via Highway 49 or 33.
plan.vehicle: Cars are standard; large RVs should verify site lengths for camping as many older loops have tight turns and overhead branches.
plan.goldenHour: Dunes Beach overlooking West Lake for sunset, where the sand takes on a deep orange hue.
